prompt:
Build a secure, robust personal substitute for Webex Meet in an empty repository.
Use Docker Compose, Jitsi Meet (or a custom WebRTC implementation), a Next.js 15 control panel, PostgreSQL, and TURN.
The core loop is: host private video calls in modest rooms, issue signed room links, and keep recordings only when every participant is clearly informed.
1. Infrastructure: Deploy via Docker Compose with a dedicated TURN service for reliable NAT traversal.
2. Owner Control Panel: Build a comprehensive admin dashboard to manage rooms, issue time-limited signed invitations, set expiry dates, toggle lobby mode (where the host admits guests), and enforce participant limits.
3. In-Meeting Experience: Implement essential collaboration features including screen sharing, a virtual whiteboard, chat, and breakout rooms. Ensure the UI is highly responsive and accessible.
4. Diagnostics: Show real-time connection diagnostics for camera, microphone, browser, bandwidth, and TURN reachability to help users troubleshoot network issues.
5. AI Assistant Integration: Integrate a local Whisper model to provide real-time transcription and closed captioning. Add functionality to generate meeting summaries from the transcript post-call.
6. Recording & Consent: Make recording disabled by default. If enabled, require an explicit on-screen consent state for every participant before recording begins. Store recordings locally with clear retention policies.
7. Security: Store room metadata and audit events securely. Implement end-to-end encryption for the media streams where possible.
Add health checks, bandwidth dashboards, backup, restore, upgrade, and incident instructions. Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states. Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs. Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path. Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps. Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane. Finish by running the tests.
